llm_response.content:
Below is a research plan I would implement given the question, data, and institutional context.

1. Identification Strategy
- Primary strategy: Difference-in-differences (DID) with an event-study to test pre-trends.
- Why DID: Both programs were rolled out to specific sets of schools at a common time (1995), with two pre-years (1993–1994) and at least two post-years (1996–1997, plus 1998 for the resources program). School-level panels and rich student microdata allow us to control for time-invariant school heterogeneity and evolving student composition.
- Multiple treatments: Estimate separate DID effects for (i) the pay-for-performance tournament and (ii) the resources+training program, in a single stacked specification. Then compare magnitudes and compute cost-effectiveness.
- Design choice for the tournament: Use the intent-to-treat (ITT) effect of being assigned to the tournament group, not ex-post “winning,” because winning is endogenous to outcomes. The treatment is the incentives regime itself.
- Augmentations:
  - Event study: Interact treatment with year dummies to visualize pre-trends and dynamics.
  - Triple-difference (DDD): Optional cross-check comparing comprehensive vs. other high schools pre/post to net out sector trends (only if needed and data support).
  - Matched DID/IPW: As a robustness check to improve treated–control comparability using pre-program observables.

2. Treatment and Control
- Unit of analysis:
  - Main: school-by-year.
  - Secondary: student-by-year (for dropout and composition-adjusted effects).
- Treatments:
  - Tournament incentives (Tourn_i): Indicator for schools assigned to the 62-school tournament group.
  - Resources+training (Res_i): Indicator for schools in the 22-school resource program.
  - If overlap exists, define mutually exclusive categories: Tournament-only, Resource-only, Both; estimate with separate interactions. Primary estimand remains ITT.
- Timing:
  - “Post” for tournament: 1995–1997. Given mid-year launch in Feb 1995, primary analyses will define Post_full_tour = 1{year ≥ 1996}; and a robustness spec uses Post_tour = 1{year ≥ 1995}.
  - “Post” for resources: 1995–1998 (program ran three years; use data through 1998 when available).
- Control group:
  - Preferred: Other comprehensive secondary schools (grades 7–12) not in either program and, where feasible, that satisfy the same uniqueness eligibility rule (only school of its type in community). This produces the most credible counterfactual.
  - Broader control (robustness): All non-participating comprehensive schools with rich controls and school and year fixed effects.
- Outcomes:
  - Achievement: average credit units, average matriculation score, average science credit units, share taking matriculation exams, share earning matriculation certificates.
  - Dropout: school-year dropout rates (grades 9–11 transitions), constructed from student IDs.

3. Key Identifying Assumptions
- Parallel trends: In the absence of the programs, treated and control schools would have evolved similarly. Plausibility:
  - The two pre-years (1993–1994) enable a pre-trend check via event-study.
  - School fixed effects absorb time-invariant differences (e.g., being the only school of its type in a community).
  - Include flexible controls for time-varying composition and local shocks (district-by-year, school-type-by-year dummies) to bolster plausibility.
- No anticipatory responses: Schools were informed and program launched in Feb 1995. With pre-years ending 1994, anticipatory changes should be limited. We will check for 1994 pre-trend breaks.
- SUTVA/no spillovers to controls: Tournament incentives apply within the treated set; direct strategic responses by control schools seem limited. We will probe by excluding nearby communities as a robustness test.
- Stable measurement of outcomes over time: National changes in matriculation standards or grading that differentially affect treated schools would violate this; year FE plus type-by-year FE mitigate this, and we will discuss any documented system-wide changes.
- Correct treatment timing and composition control: We use ITT assignment at school-year; incorporate student composition controls to mitigate composition-driven outcome changes.

4. Threats to Identification and Mitigation
- Selection into treatment:
  - Tournament eligibility is based on being the only school of its type in the community; such schools may differ systematically. Mitigation: school FE, district-by-year and school-type-by-year controls, and a control group restricted to similarly eligible schools when possible. Also test balance and pre-trends.
  - Resources program selected from applicants; selection may correlate with trends. Mitigation: same as above plus matched DID/IPW based on pre-program levels and trends in outcomes and covariates.
- Composition changes of students across schools:
  - If the incentives changed grade retention or student sorting, average outcomes may shift mechanically. Mitigation: run student-level models with rich covariates; adjust school-year aggregates by reweighting to baseline composition; show robustness of effects on cohort-fixed samples; examine intensive-margin outcomes like credits conditional on staying enrolled.
- Concurrent shocks:
  - 1990s immigration waves and local economic changes may differentially affect unique-community schools. Mitigation: include district-by-year fixed effects, student composition controls (immigrant share, parental schooling), and community-year controls if available; drop communities with large inflows in robustness analyses.
- Mid-year 1995 launch ambiguity:
  - Effects in 1995 may be attenuated or noisy. Mitigation: main estimates use 1996–1997 as “post,” with 1995 included only in event-study figures or in a robustness spec.

5. R Code Outline
Note: This is executable scaffolding. Replace file and variable names as appropriate.

# Packages
library(data.table)
library(dplyr)
library(fixest)
library(ggplot2)
library(fwildclusterboot)  # for wild-cluster bootstrap SEs

# 1) Load data
students <- fread("students_1993_1998.csv")   # student_id, school_id, year, grade, credits, avg_matric_score, sci_credits, take_matric, cert_matric, female, parent_schooling, fam_size, immigrant
schools  <- fread("schools_panel_1993_1998.csv")  # school_id, year, school_type, comprehensive, community_id, district_id, enrollment
treat    <- fread("treatment_flags.csv")  # school_id, tournament_school, resources_school

# 2) Construct school-year outcomes from student microdata
# Dropout by grade g in year t: share in school/grade in t that are not enrolled anywhere in t+1
# Keep grades 9-11 for year-to-year dropout
students <- students %>%
  filter(grade %in% 9:11) %>%
  mutate(enrolled=1L) %>%
  select(student_id, school_id, year, grade, enrolled, credits, avg_matric_score,
         sci_credits, take_matric, cert_matric, female, parent_schooling, fam_size, immigrant)

# Identify next-year enrollment anywhere
stud_next <- students %>%
  transmute(student_id, year_next = year-1L, enrolled_next = 1L)  # year-1 so we can merge by current year

students <- students %>%
  left_join(stud_next, by = c("student_id" = "student_id", "year" = "year_next")) %>%
  mutate(dropout = ifelse(is.na(enrolled_next), 1L, 0L))

# Aggregate to school-year
schyr <- students %>%
  group_by(school_id, year) %>%
  summarise(
    n_students = n(),
    avg_credits = mean(credits, na.rm=TRUE),
    avg_matric_score = mean(avg_matric_score, na.rm=TRUE),
    avg_sci_credits = mean(sci_credits, na.rm=TRUE),
    share_take_matric = mean(take_matric, na.rm=TRUE),
    share_cert_matric = mean(cert_matric, na.rm=TRUE),
    dropout_rate = mean(dropout, na.rm=TRUE),
    share_female = mean(female, na.rm=TRUE),
    avg_parent_schooling = mean(parent_schooling, na.rm=TRUE),
    avg_fam_size = mean(fam_size, na.rm=TRUE),
    share_immigrant = mean(immigrant, na.rm=TRUE)
  ) %>% ungroup()

# Merge school-year covariates and treatment
panel <- schools %>%
  filter(year >= 1993 & year <= 1998) %>%
  left_join(schyr, by = c("school_id","year")) %>%
  left_join(treat, by = "school_id") %>%
  mutate(tournament_school = ifelse(is.na(tournament_school), 0L, tournament_school),
         resources_school = ifelse(is.na(resources_school), 0L, resources_school),
         comp = ifelse(comprehensive==1L, 1L, 0L))

# Restrict to comprehensive schools for main analysis
panel_main <- panel %>%
  filter(comp==1)

# 3) Treatment timing indicators
panel_main <- panel_main %>%
  mutate(
    post_tour_full = as.integer(year >= 1996 & year <= 1997),
    post_tour_any  = as.integer(year >= 1995 & year <= 1997),
    post_res       = as.integer(year >= 1995 & year <= 1998),
    treat_tour     = tournament_school,
    treat_res      = resources_school,
    # Mutually exclusive groups if overlap exists
    tour_only      = as.integer(treat_tour==1 & treat_res==0),
    res_only       = as.integer(treat_tour==0 & treat_res==1),
    both_prog      = as.integer(treat_tour==1 & treat_res==1),
    control_none   = as.integer(treat_tour==0 & treat_res==0),
    # Optional weighting for student-weighted effects
    w_students     = ifelse(!is.na(n_students), n_students, enrollment)
  )

# 4) Main DID specification (school-by-year), ITT
# y = beta1*(treat_tour * post_tour_full) + beta2*(treat_res * post_res) + FE + controls
# Include district-by-year and school-type-by-year interactions as controls via i()
did_spec <- function(yvar) {
  fml <- as.formula(
    paste0(yvar, " ~ treat_tour:post_tour_full + treat_res:post_res + ",
           "share_female + share_immigrant + avg_parent_schooling + avg_fam_size + ",
           "i(district_id, year) + i(school_type, year) | school_id + year")
  )
  feols(fml, data = panel_main, cluster = ~ school_id, weights = ~ w_students)
}

outcomes <- c("avg_credits","avg_matric_score","avg_sci_credits","share_take_matric","share_cert_matric","dropout_rate")
did_models <- lapply(outcomes, did_spec)
names(did_models) <- outcomes
lapply(did_models, summary)

# 5) Event-study: dynamic effects and pre-trend check for tournament
# Interact treatment with year dummies, base year 1994
es_tour <- feols(
  avg_credits ~ i(year, treat_tour, ref = 1994) + treat_res:post_res +
    share_female + share_immigrant + avg_parent_schooling + avg_fam_size +
    i(district_id, year) + i(school_type, year) | school_id + year,
  data = panel_main, cluster = ~ school_id, weights = ~ w_students
)
summary(es_tour)

iplot(es_tour, ref.line = 0, xlab = "Year", main = "Tournament effects on avg_credits (event-study)")

# 6) Robustness check A: Exclude 1995 transition year, use 1993-1994 vs 1996-1997 only
panel_strict <- panel_main %>% filter(year %in% c(1993,1994,1996,1997))
rb1 <- feols(
  share_cert_matric ~ treat_tour:post_tour_full + treat_res:post_res +
    share_female + share_immigrant + avg_parent_schooling + avg_fam_size +
    i(district_id, year) + i(school_type, year) | school_id + year,
  data = panel_strict, cluster = ~ school_id, weights = ~ w_students
)
summary(rb1)

# 7) Robustness check B: School-specific linear trends
panel_main <- panel_main %>%
  group_by(school_id) %>%
  mutate(t = year - min(year, na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

rb2 <- feols(
  dropout_rate ~ treat_tour:post_tour_full + treat_res:post_res +
    share_female + share_immigrant + avg_parent_schooling + avg_fam_size +
    i(district_id, year) + i(school_type, year) | school_id + year + school_id:t,
  data = panel_main, cluster = ~ school_id, weights = ~ w_students
)
summary(rb2)

# 8) Robustness check C: Matched DID/IPW on pre-program covariates and levels
prebase <- panel_main %>% filter(year %in% c(1993,1994)) %>%
  group_by(school_id) %>%
  summarise(
    base_avg_credits = mean(avg_credits, na.rm=TRUE),
    base_share_cert = mean(share_cert_matric, na.rm=TRUE),
    base_dropout = mean(dropout_rate, na.rm=TRUE),
    base_enroll = mean(w_students, na.rm=TRUE),
    base_female = mean(share_female, na.rm=TRUE),
    base_immigrant = mean(share_immigrant, na.rm=TRUE),
    base_parent_schooling = mean(avg_parent_schooling, na.rm=TRUE),
    base_fam_size = mean(avg_fam_size, na.rm=TRUE)
  )

panel_ipw <- panel_main %>% left_join(prebase, by = "school_id")

# Propensity for being a tournament school among comprehensive controls
ps_tour <- glm(treat_tour ~ base_avg_credits + base_share_cert + base_dropout +
                 base_enroll + base_female + base_immigrant +
                 base_parent_schooling + base_fam_size +
                 factor(district_id) + factor(school_type),
               data = panel_ipw %>% filter(year==1993),
               family = binomial())

panel_ipw <- panel_ipw %>%
  mutate(phat_tour = predict(ps_tour, newdata = panel_ipw, type = "response"),
         w_ipw_tour = ifelse(treat_tour==1, 1/phat_tour, 1/(1 - phat_tour)))

rb3 <- feols(
  share_cert_matric ~ treat_tour:post_tour_full + treat_res:post_res +
    share_female + share_immigrant + avg_parent_schooling + avg_fam_size +
    i(district_id, year) + i(school_type, year) | school_id + year,
  data = panel_ipw, cluster = ~ school_id, weights = ~ w_ipw_tour
)
summary(rb3)

# 9) Inference robustness: wild-cluster bootstrap for main DID on share_cert_matric
main_model <- did_models[["share_cert_matric"]]
boot_res <- boottest(main_model, clustid = "school_id",
                     param = "treat_tour:post_tour_full", B = 9999, seed = 123)
boot_res

# 10) Cost-effectiveness back-of-the-envelope
# Suppose we estimate effect d_share_cert on share_cert_matric. Compute implied number of additional certificates per school-year and cost per additional certificate.
# Inputs (replace with actual estimates):
d_share_cert <- coef(main_model)["treat_tour:post_tour_full"]  # point estimate
avg_students_per_school <- mean(panel_main$w_students[panel_main$year %in% 1996:1997], na.rm=TRUE)
added_certs_per_schoolyr <- d_share_cert * avg_students_per_school

# Program costs (update using administrative totals):
# Tournament total awards ~ $1.44m over program; approximate annual per-school cost:
annual_tour_cost_per_school <- 1.44e6 / 2 / 62   # if 2 years of full implementation; adjust as needed
cost_per_added_cert <- annual_tour_cost_per_school / added_certs_per_schoolyr
cost_per_added_cert

6. Expected Results
- Direction: I expect positive effects of pay-for-performance on targeted achievement margins (credits, exam take-up, certificate rates) and a reduction in dropout. Tournament incentives align teacher effort with measurable outcomes and are relatively low cost; effects are likely modest but meaningful.
- Magnitudes (priors):
  - Matriculation certificate rate: +2 to +5 percentage points ITT.
  - Exam take-up: +3 to +6 percentage points.
  - Credit units and science credits: small to moderate increases (~0.05–0.10 SD).
  - Dropout: −1 to −2 percentage points.
- Relative to resources+training: I expect smaller effects per dollar for the resource program, given higher per-school spending (~$1.13–$1.15m annually over 22 schools ≈ $50k per school-year) compared to modest bonus outlays, making the tournament more cost-effective, though the resource program may still have positive impacts, particularly where baseline inputs were low.

7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)
- C1: Parallel pre-trends demonstrated in pre-period event-study (1993–1994). Score: 0.5 (only two pre-years; testable but limited power).
- C2: No anticipation before treatment (pre-1995). Score: 1 (launch Feb 1995; we exclude 1995 in main spec and test for 1994 breaks).
- C3: No spillovers/contamination to controls. Score: 0.5 (plausible; we will test by excluding nearby communities/districts).
- C4: No concurrent differentially affecting shocks. Score: 0.5 (district-year and type-year controls mitigate; immigration waves remain a concern but addressed with composition controls).
- C5: Correct treatment definition/timing and stable measurement. Score: 1 (ITT avoids endogenous “winning”; timing handled with 1996–1997 primary post).

Additional Implementation Notes
- Estimate student-level models (LPM with school and year FE, clustered at school) as a complement to school-level outcomes to ensure results are not driven by composition shifts.
- Heterogeneity: Explore effects by school-type (secular, religious boys, religious girls, Arab), baseline performance, and community size. Interact treatment with baseline quartiles.
- Multiple hypothesis correction: Where many outcomes are tested, control FDR or report standardized effect sizes.
- Presentation: Event-study plots with 95% CIs, DID coefficient tables (wild-cluster bootstrap p-values), and cost-effectiveness figures (cost per additional certificate and per SD improvement).
